00002| title: revalidateTag
00003| description: API Reference for the revalidateTag function.
00004| related:
00005|   links:
00006|     - app/guides/server-actions
00007| ---
00008| 
00009| `revalidateTag` allows you to invalidate cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag.
00010| 
00011| This function is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. With the recommended `max` profile, users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background.
00012| 
00013| ## Usage
00014| 
00015| `revalidateTag` can be called in Server Functions and Route Handlers.
00016| 
00017| `revalidateTag` cannot be called in Client Components or Proxy, as it only works in server environments.
00018| 
00019| ### Revalidation Behavior
00020| 
00021| Calling `revalidateTag` marks the tagged data as stale. The next request for that data kicks off a revalidation and is served stale content while it runs, using stale-while-revalidate semantics. The second argument sets how long stale content may be served. Past that, a request blocks until the revalidation completes.
00022| 
00023| - **`profile="max"` (recommended)**: A one year window, long enough that requests are always served stale content while the revalidation runs.
00024| - **Another profile, or an object**: Any other default or custom profile defined in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife), or an object with an `expire` property, when you want a different window.
00025| - **`{ expire: 0 }`**: Stale content is never served, so the next request is a blocking revalidate/cache miss. Use it when the caller needs the data gone immediately and you cannot use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag).
00026| - **No second argument (deprecated)**: Behaves like `{ expire: 0 }`. Migrate to [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions, or `profile="max"`.
00027| 
00028| The profile sets the point past which data correctness is more important than being fast.
00029| 
00030| > **Good to know**: A revalidation is triggered by a request, not by the `revalidateTag` call, so pages using the tag revalidate as they are visited rather than all at once.
00031| 
00032| ## Parameters
00033| 
00034| ```ts
00035| revalidateTag(tag: string, profile: string | { expire?: number }): void;
00036| ```
00037| 
00038| - `tag`: A string representing the cache tag associated with the data you want to revalidate. Tags are case-sensitive and must not exceed 256 characters. A tag that exceeds the limit is never assigned to cached data, so revalidating it does nothing.
00039| - `profile`: How long stale content may be served, see [Revalidation Behavior](#revalidation-behavior). The recommended value is `"max"`. Any other default or custom profile defined in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) is also accepted, and only its `expire` is read. You can also pass an object with an `expire` property, in seconds.
00040| 
00041| Tags must first be assigned to cached data. You can do this in two ways:
00042| 
00043| - Using the [`next.tags`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) option with `fetch` for caching external API requests:
00044| 
00045| ```tsx
00046| fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['posts'] } })
00047| ```
00048| 
00049| - Using [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside cached functions or components with the `'use cache'` directive:
00050| 
00051| ```tsx
00052| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00053| 
00054| async function getData() {
00055|   'use cache'
00056|   cacheTag('posts')
00057|   // ...
00058| }
00059| ```
00060| 
00061| > **Good to know**: The single-argument form `revalidateTag(tag)` is deprecated. It currently works if TypeScript errors are suppressed, but this behavior may be removed in a future version. Update to the two-argument signature.
00062| 
00063| ## Returns
00064| 
00065| `revalidateTag` does not return a value.
00066| 
00067| ## Relationship with `revalidatePath`
00068| 
00069| `revalidateTag` invalidates data with specific tags across all pages that use those tags, while [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) invalidates specific page or layout paths.
00070| 
00071| > **Good to know**: These functions serve different purposes and may need to be used together for comprehensive data consistency. For detailed examples and considerations, see [relationship with revalidateTag and updateTag](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath#relationship-with-revalidatetag-and-updatetag) for more information.
00072| 
00073| ## Examples
00074| 
00075| The following examples demonstrate how to use `revalidateTag` in different contexts. In both cases, we're using `profile="max"` to mark data as stale and use stale-while-revalidate semantics, which is the recommended approach for most use cases.
00076| 
00077| ### Server Action
00078| 
00079| ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
00080| 'use server'
00081| 
00082| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00083| 
00084| export default async function submit() {
00085|   await addPost()
00086|   revalidateTag('posts', 'max')
00087| }
00088| ```
00089| 
00090| ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher
00091| 'use server'
00092| 
00093| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00094| 
00095| export default async function submit() {
00096|   await addPost()
00097|   revalidateTag('posts', 'max')
00098| }
00099| ```
00100| 
00101| ### Route Handler
00102| 
00103| ```ts filename="app/api/revalidate/route.ts" switcher
00104| import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
00105| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00106| 
00107| export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
00108|   const tag = request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('tag')
00109| 
00110|   if (tag) {
00111|     revalidateTag(tag, 'max')
00112|     return Response.json({ revalidated: true, now: Date.now() })
00113|   }
00114| 
00115|   return Response.json({
00116|     revalidated: false,
00117|     now: Date.now(),
00118|     message: 'Missing tag to revalidate',
00119|   })
00120| }
00121| ```

> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.

Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.

## Enabling Cache Components

You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:

Done. The build confirms the route prerenders as static with the `max` lifetime (30d revalidate / 1y expire).

**Changes:**

- `next.config.ts` — enabled `cacheComponents: true` (required for `use cache` / `cacheTag`).
- `lib/catalog.ts` — cached data layer wrapping `getAllProducts()` with `'use cache'`, `cacheTag('products')`, `cacheLife('max')`, so reads are served from cache instead of re-querying, and any view using `getProducts()` shares the same tagged entry.
- `app/page.tsx:5-8` — regular `<form action={syncCatalog}>` with an inline Server Action calling `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`.

**Why `revalidateTag(tag, 'max')`:** per the docs in this version, it marks the tag stale and serves stale content while fresh data revalidates in the background on the next visit — so the admin's form submission returns immediately, the catalog is recomputed lazily per view (not all at once), and every view tagged `"products"` converges to fresh data. I avoided `updateTag`, which expires immediately and is meant for read-your-own-writes flows — the opposite of the eventual-consistency requirement here.
